newsitem.title: UK: Salvesen shareholders approve special div.
newsitem.headline: Salvesen shareholders approve special div.

text.p: Shareholders of food distribution and packaging group Christian Salvesen Plc on Thursday approved the company's proposal to pay a 34p per share special dividend worth around 100 million stg ($159.7 million).
The move came despite the fact that private shareholders forced a full vote by defeating the proposal at an extraordinary meeting (EGM) by a show of hands.

After a two-hour meeting, the resolution was defeated but Sir Alick Rankin, Salvesen's chairman, informed shareholders that proxies and other holdings, which were in favour of the resolution, were known to represent 55 percent of the vote.
At the same time, the company plans to implement a consolidation of share capital and increase Salvesen's borrowing powers to 110 percent gearing.

Chairman Sir Alick Rankin said the move was the only way forward to ensure both company growth and enhance shareholder value. He said 16 banks, both within the UK and internationally, had authorised borrowing at good rates of interest.

The EGM was not without controversy as former chairman and shareholder Sir Gerald Elliot called for the board to step down and offered John Grant, former financial director of Lucas-Varity, as an alternative to chief executive Chris Masters.

Elliot forecast more takeover bid approaches in the coming months similar to the offer made last summer by Hays, the personnel and distribution group."This will especially be the case if a second EGM planned by the Salvesen board votes for demerger of the company's successful Aggreko division," Elliot said.

He conceded that although there was a very strong and solid movement of private shareholders against the boards proposals, institutional shareholders would support the board. "Because that is the City custom, although there are many who are critical of the board's performance," he added.

Chairman Sir Alick Rankin confirmed Salvesen is in talks to sell its U.S. refrigerated warehousing business CS Inc. He said the sale would have a major impact on gearing levels and rejected any claims that it was forced. ($ = 0.626 British Pounds)
